title: Narrow the model's tools per stage, and say so to the user and the model
action: FINISH THE OTHER HALF. The belt side of this cell is already committed at b2cc78ddf and is correct in shape: it calls runAdvisoryHook(directory, "stage-tools", ...) instead of hardcoding a stage table, registers /bee-tools-reopen, and notifies the user. But bee has no such hook: `bee hook stage-tools` answers `unknown hook "stage-tools"` and exits 1, so the advisory wrapper swallows it and the gate narrows NOTHING. The feature is inert today. Do not redo the belt work; add the answering side. One: add "stage-tools" to HOOK_NAMES in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/hooks/mod.rs — note the array length is declared, so the count changes too — and route it to a new hooks/stage_tools.rs module beside the existing hook modules, following whatever shape those already use for reading stdin and writing a JSON verdict. Two: the hook answers, for the feature's CURRENT phase, which tools are allowed. Keep the mapping small, explicit and in Rust where bee's other rules live: before the execution gate is approved the model gets read-only tools; after it, the full set. Read how the write-guard hook already decides phase and gate state and reuse that, rather than inventing a second reader. Three: the answer must carry, alongside the allowed tool names, a short human sentence the belt shows the USER and a short sentence it gives the MODEL naming stage policy as the reason (per D12) — the belt already expects both, so match what it reads. Four: prove it end to end, not just in unit tests. Run `bee hook stage-tools` with a real payload and show it returns a verdict rather than `unknown hook`. A test that only asserts the belt SOURCE contains the call is exactly the trap this cell already fell into once. Finally, .pi/extensions is a root the release manifest hashes: re-run bee dev regen (render-skill-trees, then onboard --repo-root . --apply, then release-manifest --write) if the belt changes again, and keep bee dev release-manifest --check in the proof.
